subject: physics
title: Hadrons, leptons and quarks
key_idea: Matter particles are either hadrons, which feel the strong interaction and are made of quarks, or leptons, which are fundamental. Baryons contain three quarks and mesons contain a quark and an antiquark. Up, down and strange quarks have charges of +⅔e, −⅓e and −⅓e.

blocks.text: Particles that feel the strong interaction are hadrons. Particles that do not are leptons or photons.

items.meaning: A particle made of quarks, which feels the strong nuclear force.
A hadron made of three quarks, such as the proton and neutron.
A hadron made of one quark and one antiquark, such as the pion and kaon.
A fundamental particle that does not feel the strong force, such as the electron and neutrino.

items: All hadrons are affected by both the strong and the weak nuclear force.
All leptons are affected by the weak force but **not** the strong force.
Leptons are fundamental: they are not made of anything smaller.
Hadrons are not fundamental: they are made of quarks.
Every particle has an antiparticle, so there are antibaryons and antileptons as well.

items: Hadrons (baryons and mesons) feel the strong force and are made of quarks.
Leptons are fundamental and do not feel the strong force.

blocks.text: A quark is a fundamental particle. There are six flavours: up, down, strange, charm, top and bottom. Every quark has an antiquark.

items: An antiquark has the opposite charge to its quark.
e is the elementary charge, 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
Charges of hadrons are the sum of the charges of their quarks, and are whole numbers of e.
Up has +⅔e. Down and strange have −⅓e.
Antiquarks have the opposite charge.

blocks.text: A baryon is three quarks. A meson is a quark and an antiquark. Add the charges to check each answer.

items: Proton uud, neutron udd.
Mesons are a quark and an antiquark, such as π⁺ = u d̄.
The total charge of the quarks is the charge of the hadron.

checks.q: State the quark composition of a proton and a neutron.
checks.a: Proton: up, up, down (uud). Neutron: up, down, down (udd).

checks.q: A meson is made of an up quark and an anti-down quark. Show that its charge is +1e and state whether it is a baryon, a meson or a lepton.
checks.a: Charge = +⅔e + (+⅓e) = +1e. It is a meson: a hadron made of a quark and an antiquark.

checks.q: State two differences between hadrons and leptons.
checks.a: Hadrons are made of quarks and feel the strong nuclear force. Leptons are fundamental particles and do not feel the strong force.

items: The proton is the only stable baryon. Other baryons eventually decay into it.
The pion is the exchange particle of the strong nuclear force. The kaon can decay into pions.
Leptons include the electron, the muon and the electron and muon neutrinos, and their antiparticles.
The muon decays into an electron.
**Baryon number** is a quantum number. Baryons have +1, antibaryons −1 and everything else 0.
**Lepton number** is a quantum number. Leptons have +1 and antileptons −1. Electron and muon lepton numbers are each conserved.
Particle physics relies on large teams of scientists and engineers to validate new knowledge.
Strange particles, such as kaons, are produced through the strong interaction but decay through the weak interaction.
They are always created in pairs. This is shown by a quantum number called **strangeness** (symbol s).
Strangeness is conserved in strong interactions. It can change by 0, +1 or −1 in weak interactions.

blocks.text: An antiquark has the opposite value of each property. The neutron decays by changing a d quark to a u quark: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄.

items: In the standard quark–lepton model, particles are classified as baryons, mesons, leptons and photons.
Photons are particles of electromagnetic radiation. They are neither hadrons nor leptons.
The symmetry of the model predicted the top quark before it was found.

blocks.text: The antiquark of each flavour has the opposite charge. No other quark properties are needed.
